observation: Three BPM stations show a correlated, sustained beam disturbance. LTUH:250:X exhibits a large position excursion (peak_robust_z 62.49, 42 consecutive samples) beginning at 1604277200689428941. Approximately 8.26 ms later, at 1604277200697686480, three co-located charge monitors (LTUH:450:TMIT z=78.69, DMPH:502:TMIT z=43.35, DMPH:693:TMIT z=5.11) all register sustained TMIT drops with 301 consecutive samples and ~300 low-charge flags, while their position channels (LTUH:450:X z=59.81, DMPH:502:Y z=20.21, DMPH:693:Y z=11.50) show large deviations with ~300-301 invalid position samples at the same onset. The candidate RF station KLYS:LI29:11 reports a 99.96% amplitude peak deviation, but with 97% no-update fraction, only 20 finite updates, and only 1 of 82 neighbors independently flagged. Data quality at the BPMs is adequate (full 120 Hz coverage, no nonfinite values).

KLYS:LI29:11 amplitude dropped from baseline ~69.12 to ~0.024 (99.96% deviation) at recorded time 1604277203201922048 ns, recovering ~5 s later. Multiple downstream BPMs (BPMS:DMPH:502, BPMS:DMPH:693, BPMS:LTUH:450) show sustained low-charge episodes (300–301 samples) beginning ~1604277200697686480 ns, with charge-valid TMIT excursions (peak_robust_z up to 78.69). However, BPMS:LTUH:250:X (upstream of LI29 in the linac) shows a sustained position excursion (peak_robust_z 62.49, 42 samples) without an associated low-charge TMIT excursion, indicating beam disturbance was present upstream of LI29:11. RF reporting is asynchronous with up to ~5 s delay and no RF phase data is available.

KLYS:LI28:11:AMPL showed a single finite excursion to 32.93 (~38.8% below baseline median 53.83) at 1604278211445212672, recovering ~4.99 s later to 53.81. Four BPM position channels (DMPH:502:Y, DMPH:693:Y, LTUH:250:X, LTUH:450:X) showed sustained excursions with robust z-scores 16.6-38.9 over 11-17 consecutive samples, all onsets at 1604278210729114201 (~0.71 s before the recorded RF timestamp). Charge-valid beam evidence corroborates a sustained position disturbance. Of 82 RF columns, only KLYS:LI28:11 was flagged suspicious; 28 neighboring columns had unknown baselines and could not be evaluated.

Beam position disturbance corroborated at onset 1604278210729114201 by simultaneous sustained deviations in LTU X-position channels (BPMS:LTUH:250:X z≈38.9, BPMS:LTUH:450:X z≈37.7; 17 consecutive samples each) and Dump Y-position channels (BPMS:DMPH:502:Y z≈26.4 over 15 samples, BPMS:DMPH:693:Y z≈16.6 over 11 samples). All four position channels share the identical onset timestamp. TMIT channels at all four BPMs show only modest non-sustained z-scores (1.7–5.6) with no charge loss, indicating charge-valid beam position evidence. Candidate RF station KLYS:LI28:11:AMPL shows ~38.8% peak deviation but with severely degraded data (96.9% no-update fraction, 65,800 nonfinite values against 813 samples, only 1 of 82 neighbors flagged), which is insufficient to establish it as the unique cause of the observed beam disturbance.

Reconciliation across rf, dump (DMPH 502/693), and ltu (LTUH 250/450) nodes for candidate window on station KLYS:LI21:81. RF channel shows a modest ~2.9% peak deviation but is dominated by sparse updates (~98.7% no-update fraction, only 11 finite samples) and anomalous data-quality flags (66,449 nonfinite values over 821 samples, with 28/82 neighboring baselines unknown), preventing a reliable RF-side characterization. Both BPM groups report adequate data quality (no nonfinite values, full 120 Hz fraction) with no sustained anomalies (longest_consecutive_samples = 0 on every channel) and no identifiable onset; the dump and LTU robust-z excursions are isolated (BPMS:DMPH:502:Y peak 4.43, BPMS:DMPH:502:TMIT peak 3.29, BPMS:LTUH:450:TMIT peak 4.04, BPMS:LTUH:450:X peak 4.01, BPMS:LTUH:250:TMIT peak 3.93, BPMS:LTUH:250:X peak 3.61, BPMS:DMPH:693:Y peak 3.48, BPMS:DMPH:693:TMIT peak 2.24). No temporal alignment between an RF excursion onset and any BPM onset can be made; no RF phase data is available.

Candidate KLYS:LI21:81 shows a modest amplitude excursion at the candidate endpoint (73.24 vs baseline 75.44, ~2.91% deviation), with only 2 RF updates in the ~60s window. No sustained or threshold-crossing beam disturbance was detected on any of the 4 TMIT channels or 4 position channels in the BPM evidence; all peak robust-z scores remained well below the 6σ heuristic threshold and longest consecutive excursions were 0. No neighboring klystron station in the available 82 columns was flagged suspicious. Charge is healthy on all BPMs (no low-charge or invalid-position samples). Only the candidate-end RF update is anomalous; the next update ~5s later returns to baseline.

KLYS:LI21:81:AMPL shows a single small excursion of ~1.4% (75.439 -> 74.365) at the candidate timestamp, with recovery to 75.415 ~5s later. RF updates are extremely sparse (13/769 finite samples, ~98.3% no-update fraction). Across all 8 BPM channels (4 TMIT + 4 position), no sustained beam disturbance is detected: peak robust z-scores range 2.50-4.29 (all below the 6-sigma threshold), no TMIT drops below 1e8, no low-charge or invalid-position samples, and longest_consecutive_samples=0 for every channel. 28 of 82 RF columns have unknown baselines, so neighboring-station uniqueness cannot be established. Documented RF reporting delay is approximate (0-5 s); no fixed timing is inferred.

RF station KLYS:LI21:81:AMPL is starved of data within the candidate window (~98.3% no-update fraction; only 3 finite updates, 62237 non-finite values) with a modest 1.42% peak deviation and only 1/82 neighbor columns flagged suspicious, so no clear RF amplitude excursion is established. Both BPM instruments report good data quality (full 120 Hz, zero non-finite values, zero low-charge or invalid-position samples) but transient peak robust-z excursions (LTUH ~3.7-4.3; DMPH ~2.5-4.2, notably BPMS:DMPH:693:Y ~4.18) without persistence, no consecutive anomalous samples, and no onsets returned by the disturbance detectors; the LTU node therefore reports 'normal' while the dump node reports 'insufficient_evidence' for sustained disturbance.
